text: What name was Augustus born with before his adoption by Julius Caesar?
How was Octavian related to Julius Caesar by blood before adoption?
What transformed Octavian into Caesar's legal son and heir?
choices: Caesar's posthumous adoption in his will

text: In what year did the Senate grant Octavian the title Augustus?
The title princeps was meant to suggest that Augustus was what?
Which political arrangement is usually called the First Constitutional Settlement of Augustus?
choices: The grant of censorship for life
The apparent return of powers in 27 BCE paired with control of key provinces
The division of Italy into four prefectures
The annexation of Egypt to the Senate

text: The Second Constitutional Settlement of 23 BCE is especially associated with Augustus receiving what enduring powers?
choices: Tribunician power and greater proconsular imperium

text: What did tribunicia potestas give Augustus without making him an actual tribune of the plebs?
choices: Control of the treasury at Saturn's temple
The right to crown client kings
The command of the Praetorian Guard
Sacrosanctity and powers associated with the tribunate

text: Imperium maius allowed Augustus to do what in relation to other governors?
Which battle in 31 BCE broke the power of Antony and Cleopatra?
What city fell to Octavian in 30 BCE, ending the last war of the Roman Republic?
Which member of the Second Triumvirate was eventually pushed aside after his failed power play in Sicily?
Sextus Pompey was most dangerous to Octavian because he controlled which island base?
Which famous orator was killed during the triumviral proscriptions?
At the Battle of Philippi in 42 BCE, Octavian and Antony defeated which pair of Caesar's assassins?
Who was Augustus's closest military lieutenant and the victor at Actium?
Who is most closely associated with literary patronage under Augustus?
Which woman became Augustus's influential wife and the mother of Tiberius?
Who was Augustus's only biological child?
Who ultimately succeeded Augustus as princeps in 14 CE?
Which young relative of Augustus died in 23 BCE after being treated as a likely heir?
Which pair of Augustus's adopted grandsons were prominently prepared for succession before dying young?
The disaster of 9 CE in Germania is chiefly associated with the destruction of the forces of which Roman commander?
Which monument celebrated Augustan peace and was dedicated in 9 BCE?
What is the Res Gestae Divi Augusti?
choices: An inscriptional summary of Augustus's achievements

text: Which poet under Augustus wrote the Aeneid?
Which Augustan poet was eventually exiled to Tomis on the Black Sea?
The Carmen Saeculare performed at the Secular Games of 17 BCE was written by whom?
The marriage legislation associated with Augustus aimed chiefly to do what?
choices: Promote lawful marriage and childbearing among the elite

text: What did the Julian adultery law do that was especially striking in Roman terms?
choices: It made adultery a public criminal offense
It allowed women to vote in assemblies

text: Which honor was awarded to Augustus in 2 BCE as father of the Roman community?
After Lepidus died, which chief priesthood did Augustus finally assume in 12 BCE?
The closing of the gates of Janus under Augustus symbolized what?
choices: The founding of a new colony

text: What was the Praetorian Guard in the Augustan system?
choices: An elite force for the princeps's protection
A priestly college for imperial cult

text: What was the aerarium militare established by Augustus?
choices: A temple treasury for Mars Ultor
A reserve fund for senatorial loans
A military treasury for veterans' discharge payments

text: How did Augustus commonly deal with demobilized veterans after the civil wars?
choices: He immediately recalled them to service
He settled all of them inside Rome
He turned them into tax collectors
He settled many in colonies and granted rewards

text: After the defeat of Cleopatra, Egypt held what special status under Augustus?
choices: It became an imperial province under his personal control
It remained an independent allied kingdom
It was handed to the Senate as a peaceful province

text: Who usually governed Roman Egypt under Augustus?
What notable diplomatic success did Augustus achieve with Parthia in 20 BCE?
choices: He recovered Roman standards lost by Crassus
He installed himself as king of Parthia

text: Augustus's eastern policy toward Parthia is best described as what?
choices: A relentless program of full conquest
A preference for diplomacy and client-king management over direct conquest

text: Which Judaean ruler functioned as an important client king during the age of Augustus?
What major building dominated the Forum of Augustus?
Which famous boast is traditionally attributed to Augustus about Rome?
choices: He found it conquered and left it peaceful
He found it wooden and left it golden
He found it brick and left it marble
He found it pagan and left it sacred

text: In his role as moral and religious renewer, Augustus claimed to have restored approximately how many temples in Rome?
Under Augustus, the Roman world was broadly divided administratively into which two kinds of provinces?
Which body did Augustus repeatedly revise and reduce in size to make it more manageable?
Why was Augustus's resignation of the annual consulship in 23 BCE important?
choices: It made him a private citizen
It transferred the empire to Agrippa
It let him dominate without monopolizing the consulship every year
It abolished the office of consul

text: What urban force did Augustus create to help maintain public order in Rome?
Which Augustan force became especially associated with firefighting and nighttime policing in Rome?
Augustus is often credited with reducing abuses in provincial taxation by limiting the power of whom?
What administrative tool was central to assessing tribute in many provinces under Augustus?
Coins showing Augustus with symbols of victory, peace, or divine favor primarily served what purpose?
choices: They replaced all local currencies at once
They worked as a form of imperial propaganda
They were used only inside temples

text: The star or comet linked to Caesar in Octavian's propaganda signified what claim?
choices: That the Sibyls backed the Triumvirate

text: What does the title Divi Filius mean when used by Augustus?
What city did Octavian found near the site of his victory at Actium?
About how many legions did Augustus leave as the core of Rome's standing army after his settlements?
What important reward commonly awaited auxiliary soldiers after honorable service under the early Principate?
Which frontier line became especially important in Augustus's long-term strategic outlook?
After the Varian disaster, what happened to the project of turning Germania into a stable Roman province east of the Rhine?
choices: It was transferred to Cleopatra Selene
It was handed to the Senate

text: Which long conflict in northern Spain occupied Augustus's regime earlier in his reign?
Which Anatolian kingdom became the Roman province of Galatia during Augustus's rise to power?
Which major revolt from 6 to 9 CE severely tested Augustan power in the Balkans before the Teutoburg disaster?
Where did Augustus die in 14 CE?
What happened to Augustus after his death in official state religion?
choices: He was condemned by the Senate
He was remembered only as consul

text: Which biographer wrote a surviving Life of Augustus in the imperial period?
Which later historian wrote in Greek and provides an important narrative of Augustus's reign in Roman History?
Which historian begins the Annals with a darkly skeptical account of Augustus's accumulation of power?
Modern historians usually use which term for the political order founded by Augustus?
Augustus's claim to have 'restored the Republic' is treated by many historians chiefly as what?
choices: A literal return to pre-Sullan politics
A slogan invented only by Tacitus

text: Which phrase best captures the difference between Augustus's auctoritas and his formal potestas?
choices: Auctoritas was legal office, potestas was family prestige
Auctoritas was influence and prestige beyond formal office
Auctoritas was another word for kingship

text: Why was the date of a princeps's tribunician power useful in Roman imperial documents?
choices: It served as a dating formula for his reign

text: The Lex Papia Poppaea of 9 CE is best understood as what?
choices: A law ending slavery for debt
A supplement to Augustan marriage legislation

text: Augustus reorganized neighborhood cult in Rome by linking the Lares Compitales with whose genius?
Which Roman month was renamed Augustus in his honor?
What major religious festival did Augustus celebrate in 17 BCE to mark a renewed era for Rome?
What group increasingly supplied many imperial administrators and prefects under Augustus?
Which office under Augustus became especially important for supervising Rome's grain supply?
Before Tiberius concentrated them more heavily near Rome, Augustus often stationed Praetorian cohorts where?
Which victory over Sextus Pompey in 36 BCE was won by Agrippa and helped secure Octavian's west?
Which phrase best describes Octavian's public image after his victory in the civil wars?
choices: A restorer of peace and traditional order

text: Which female relative of Augustus was famously used in dynastic marriage politics and later exiled for scandal?
Which public work in Rome is especially associated with Agrippa's building activity under Augustus?
Which historian was a near-contemporary of Augustus and wrote a vast history of Rome from its origins?
Which phrase was not a normal public title of Augustus and would have sounded too monarchical for his image?
What was the main purpose of Augustus's Mausoleum in Rome?
choices: A dynastic tomb for his family line
A records office for the Senate

text: Which close associate of Augustus briefly fell from favor and later died after a disastrous command in the east?
Which region was turned into a province in 6 CE after the deposition of Archelaus?
Which member of Augustus's family was known for major campaigns in Germany before dying in 9 BCE?
Which branch of government continued to meet and pass decrees under Augustus, even as real power shifted toward the princeps?
Which term best captures the way Augustus handled succession?
choices: Dynastic preparation without a formal hereditary law

text: Which claim did Augustan art and ideology often make about his rule?
choices: That Rome should become a democracy again
That civil war was glorious in itself
That Augustus brought a new golden age

text: Which phrase best describes the Augustan settlement according to many modern scholars?
choices: A complete end to aristocratic politics
A pure military dictatorship with no civilian forms
A monarchy concealed beneath republican institutions

text: Which document of Augustus is especially valuable because it presents his own preferred version of his career?
Which colony in Hispania is named for Augustus and his veterans?
What office did Augustus carefully avoid accepting despite repeated emergencies, because it carried strong memories of republican collapse?
Which sea victory helped make possible Octavian's final showdown with Antony?
Which statement about Augustus's rule would most likely fit the view of the sympathetic historian Velleius Paterculus?
choices: It rescued the state from chaos
It was simply another tyranny no different from Nero's
It destroyed every Roman institution instantly

text: Which relative of Augustus married Mark Antony and is often remembered as a symbol of dignified dynastic politics?
Which phrase best explains why Augustus's coin portraits mattered politically?
choices: They were illegal in the provinces
They spread his image and messages across the empire

text: What was unusual about Egypt in the Augustan order from the perspective of Roman senators?
choices: Senators could not enter it freely without permission

text: Which campaign slogan-like idea linked Augustus with both peace and victory rather than with simple retreat from war?
choices: Peace through conquest ended in order

text: Which office holder under Augustus was responsible for managing Rome's waters and aqueduct system after Agrippa's reforms?
Which pair best represents the two principal heirs adopted by Augustus after the death of Agrippa?
Which description best fits Augustus's use of religion in politics?
choices: He separated religion from state more than any Roman leader
He used religious restoration to legitimize his rule
